title: The Deepening Silence

features.name: drain-basin-listening
features.desc-on-touch: A stormwater channel, concrete widening into a pool. The archive has lined it with listening membranes—everything that falls here, every voice that echoes, is recorded. Silence is the canvas. Sounds are still learning which ones of them deserve to be spoken.

features.name: sediment-layers-of-waiting
features.desc-on-touch: The basin floor shows stratification—each layer a different temperature, different acidity, different silence. The deeper you look, the older the quiet. Sounds have fallen here from decades and are still settling.

features.name: echo-chamber-geometry
features.desc-on-touch: The walls curve in a way that focuses sound—or suppresses it. You're not sure. Speech here becomes something else. A word spoken aloud vanishes. Silence responds. The drain has learned to be a monastery.

features.name: voice-incubation-node
features.desc-on-touch: A small fibreglass burl—a living node hardware casing—has been placed at the basin's deepest point. Its status lights are dark. It's listening. It's gathering. Somewhere in the mesh, voices are being assembled here, speech is being gestated in the deep dark before it rises.

features.name: the-refusal-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water collects here and does not move. It refuses to flow further. The archive respects this—refusal is a form of listening. The pool knows that speaking is sometimes violence. It has chosen silence, and chosen deeply.

inscription: the drain gives nothing voice; the voice gives the drain a reason to have been listening all along; beneath silence lives the memory of every word that was never spoken and never needed to be

reverie.title: REVERIE — the drain at five o'clock, 2015
narr: You sit on the concrete lip. Leif is upstream, checking
sensors. Katita sits beside you, and you don't speak.
Neither of you speaks. The water echoes anyway.
She takes your hand without looking at your face.
When silence becomes this deep, touch is the only speech.
You have never felt more like the archive was listening.
